en.headline: Wan Chai Blue House hangs 700 hand-painted Mid-Autumn lanterns
en.dek: The cluster on Stone Nullah Lane lights up from 6pm to 9.30pm until 14 October, stretching into nearby side streets.
body: More than 700 hand-painted lanterns are on display around Wan Chai's Blue House cluster through Mid-Autumn Festival and into mid-October, lighting the tong lau and adjoining lanes each evening.

Organiser Viva Blue House said residents, neighbours, pet owners and about 50 local illustrators painted the lanterns. The display runs along Stone Nullah Lane, Kat On Street, Hing Wan Street, King Sing Street and Queen's Road East. Lights are switched on from 6pm to 9.30pm daily until 14 October.

The group said the project began during the pandemic as a community effort to bring people back onto the streets, and this is the fifth year the cluster has been dressed for the festival. The Blue House at 72 Stone Nullah Lane remains a lived-in heritage building under a "retain the building, retain the people" conservation approach.
Admission is free. Mid-Autumn Festival falls on Friday 25 September, with a general holiday the following day.

zh.headline: 灣仔藍屋掛出700盎手繪中秋花燈
zh.dek: 石水渠街建築群花燈展期至10月14日，每晚6時至9時半亮燈，並延伸至附近橫街。
body: 灣仔藍屋建築群一帶掛出逾700盎手繪花燈，展期涵蓋中秋至10月中，每晚點亮舊唐樓及鄰近街巷。
主辦單位「嘩藍屋」表示，花燈由街坊、鄰居、寵物主人和約50名本地插畫家繪製，範圍包括石水渠街、吉安街、慶雲街、景星街及皇后大道東，每晚6時至9時半亮燈，直至10月14日。
單位指活動源自疫情期間希望把人重新帶回街上的社區構想，今年是連續第五年為中秋掛燈。石水渠街72號藍屋仍是有人居住的活化歷史建築，沿用「留屋留人」方針。
參觀免費。中秋正日為9月25日星期五，翌日為公眾假期。
